newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cotton weekly export sales highlights -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cotton weekly export sales highlights -- USDA.

text.p: Net Upland sales of 19,100 running bales (RB) were two-fifths below the previous week, but exceeded the 4-week average by four-fifths. Major increases for China (6,600 RB), Russia (4,400 RB), Mexico (2,000 RB), and Ecuador (1,900 RB) were partially offset by reductions of 2,100 RB for Hong Kong.
Sales of 166,400 RB for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year were primarily for Mexico (64,400 RB), Colombia (22,000 RB), Brazil (17,000 RB), Canada (13,800 RB), and China (11,200 RB).

Exports of 151,500 RB were 61 percent above the previous week and 31 percent more than the 4-week average. West European destinations accounted for 37 percent of the week's shipments; Western Hemisphere, 32 percent; and Asian, 31 percent. The major recipients were Turkey (54,800 RB), Mexico (34,300 RB), and China (21,400 RB).
